title: WHY MEERKATS TAKE TURNS WATCHING FOR DANGER
caption: A meerkat lookout is part of a team strategy. 🐾 #Meerkat #AnimalBehavior #Wildlife #WildVox

narration_timeline.text: Why do meerkats stay together when they move across open ground?
narration_timeline.scene: Real meerkat group walking or gathered; no invented predator.

narration_timeline.text: In the wild, they live in social groups that share space and burrows.
narration_timeline.scene: Captive meerkat family illustrates group structure; do not claim zoo footage is wild.

narration_timeline.text: One meerkat may stand upright and scan while its neighbors search for food.
narration_timeline.scene: Documented upright, scanning meerkat at Ueno Zoo, without claiming visible foraging neighbors.

narration_timeline.text: A lookout can notice approaching danger and give the group time to react.
narration_timeline.scene: Meerkat group footage; no invented alarm call or predator event.

narration_timeline.text: As the group moves, different individuals can take turns watching their surroundings.
narration_timeline.scene: Two distinct real meerkat group clips, no implication of same continuous event.

narration_timeline.text: So that famous upright pose is part of teamwork, not just a cute photo.
narration_timeline.scene: Meerkat family and sentry-context group activity; two distinct authentic clips.
